Use `snl library remove-entry` to remove one Library occurrence without deleting the underlying Entry.

### Availability
This Entry is a normative product contract. The command is implemented only when its canonical path appears in machine-readable `snl --help`; absence means planned and unavailable, never silently emulated through a different command.


### Command path
`library/remove-entry` is the canonical transport-neutral command. The intended shell spelling is `snl library remove-entry`. Current availability is advertised by machine-readable `snl --help`; an Agent/MCP adapter submits the same operation object instead of reconstructing shell text.

### Operation request
```json
{"protocol":"snl.operation/v1","command":"library/remove-entry","root":"/absolute/workspace","arguments":{"id":"<library-slug>","occurrenceId":"<exact-occurrence-id>","expectedRevision":"<opaque>"}}
```
Every adapter accepts exactly this semantic request. Unknown argument keys are rejected. The CLI accepts `--root` and `--json` globally and emits one complete JSON document followed by a newline. `occurrenceId` is required and uniquely selects the occurrence to detach. `entryId`, parent, and ordering selectors are rejected because they cannot disambiguate duplicate occurrences and do not affect removal.

### Success result
A successful call exits `0` and returns `{"protocol":"snl.result/v1","ok":true,"command":"library/remove-entry","data":{},"diagnostics":[]}`. `data` contains the changed occurrence and canonical Library readback with new revision.

### Failure and exit semantics
Domain rejection (invalid data, not-found, conflict, or validation errors) exits `1`. Invocation, input I/O, unsupported workspace/schema, lock acquisition, and runtime failures exit `2`. Failure stdout under `--json` is exactly one `{"protocol":"snl.result/v1","ok":false,"command":"library/remove-entry","error":{"code":"<stable-code>","message":"<actionable text>","details":{},"retryable":false}}`; no stack trace or prose contaminates stdout.

### State and concurrency
Mutating. Bind Library revision under the shared lock, validate node/edge identities and projected acyclic topology, then durably publish all graph files together or roll back. Revisions, cursors, checked digests, and workspace revisions are opaque tokens. After success, canonical readback and whole-workspace validation must observe the published state.
